name: NY-10
label: Safe D

key_factors: Lander's strong fundraising and name recognition as NYC official
Republican nominee has no reported fundraising
model.rationale: This Brooklyn-based seat carries a +32 Democratic lean, and the Democratic nominee Brad Lander has raised $2.5 million while the Republican nominee shows no reported fundraising. Markets price a Democratic win near certainty, so the race stays Safe D.
model.watch: A surprise third-party or independent surge, or an unusually low-turnout primary fallout, could narrow the margin but is very unlikely to flip the seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Dan Goldman (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Dan Goldman lost renomination, leaving this heavily Democratic Brooklyn seat open, but the Democratic nominee Brad Lander enters as a clear favorite. Lander, a prominent citywide officeholder, raised about $2.5 million for the race, while Republican nominee Jennifer Moore reports no fundraising on file. Prediction markets put the Democratic side near 98%, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive.

The district's +32 Democratic partisan lean makes a general-election upset implausible even with an open seat. The main uncertainty is the size of the margin, not the winner, since Lander's primary victory could leave some factions less engaged in November.
